metaDescription: How to hire for deck and fence staining in Ontario, from pressure-washing and sanding prep to picking a dry weather window that actually lasts.
intro: Staining is one of those jobs where the prep matters more than the product, since a stain applied over dirty or damp wood tends to peel within a season regardless of brand. Timing also counts in Ontario, since the wood needs a stretch of dry, moderate weather to cure properly.
whatToLookFor: A clear pressure-washing and sanding process before any stain goes on
Willingness to check wood moisture content rather than staining on a schedule
Experience matching stain type, oil or water-based, to the existing finish
A realistic plan around Ontario's spring and fall dry weather windows
Sample boards or references showing how a past job looks a year or two later
typicalCostNotes: Pricing usually scales with square footage and how much sanding or old-finish removal the wood needs, so a deck or fence that only needs a light clean and one coat costs less than one with peeling paint or years of buildup to strip. Two-coat applications and larger multi-level decks push the price up, and rescheduling around a dry-weather window can affect timing more than cost.
questionsToAsk: How many dry days in a row do you need before and after staining?
What is your pressure-washing PSI and drying time before sanding?
Will you test the wood moisture level before applying stain?
Is this an oil-based or water-based product, and why for my wood?
How many coats are included, and what happens if weather delays the second coat?
redFlags: Plans to stain immediately after pressure-washing with no drying time
No process for sanding or removing old, failing finish first
Will stain in rain-threatened or high-humidity conditions to keep the schedule
